edit.description: two row walks beside the phase-declaration ones, over the refusal-context and order-context tables

summary: the authoring page's refusal-context and order-context tables are walked against the interfaces they row, the way the phase-declaration tables already are

per.section: A seam gate reads what the real writer wrote

acceptance: each of the two tables is read against its interface's own declaration order by the same walk the phase-declaration tables use, so a field gained, a row dropped, or a row out of order reds on one equality rather than waiting for a reader to notice
pins: the authoring page's refusal-context table rows every field the refusal context declares
the authoring page's order-context table rows every field the order context declares
notes: Measured by the tick that pinned the phase-declaration tables: both tables row all four fields their interfaces declare today and neither is pinned, so this is two reader cases and no row work — the reader and the section walk are both in place (`tests/helpers/docSections.ts`, `tests/helpers/docWalk.ts`). The unpinned optionality claim beside them needs a widening of the walk's result nothing else wants yet and stays out. Collides with the gate-context entry on this file.
